title: MarketAdmission
description: The PRE-BOOK ADMISSION verdict (roadmap 4.5). Before a book is opened — before a single chapter is drafted — this read-side check asks the commercial questions the North Star demands: is the target reader defined, is there a real pay trigger, is the book differentiated, does it have a first-30-chapter hook and 100-chapter sustainability. It is a DETERMINISTIC FOLD of three inputs the project already holds: the authored Market Position (sources/market-position.yaml), the authored Novel Brain (sources/novel-brain.yaml), and the derived Market Snapshot (registry/derived/market/). It introduces no new judgment model — every check is a deterministic read of those artifacts, so the same inputs always yield the same verdict (fixture-validated, no live model needed). Written to registry/derived/market-admission/, NEVER to registry/facts/ (an admission verdict is not a story fact, ADR-006). Two structural invariants: `gating` const false — admission NEVER blocks a build (ADR-003), it advises whether opening the book is commercially sound; and `authority` const human — opening/committing to a book is an outward, hard-to-reverse decision (ADR-009), so the system may recommend but only a human commits.

authority.description: Structural invariant (ADR-009): committing to write a book is an outward, hard-to-reverse decision, so only a human makes it. This artifact stages a recommendation, never auto-admits.

gating.description: Structural invariant (ADR-003): a market-admission verdict NEVER blocks a build. It is advisory positioning intelligence, not a deterministic build gate.

recommendation.description: admit = positioning is commercially sound, open the book; revise = fixable gaps in the positioning, sharpen before opening (soft); hold = positioning is incomplete or internally contradictory, do not open yet.

completeness.description: Does the positioning actually answer the pre-book questions? A missing pay_trigger / first_30_hook / sustainability_100 (or an absent Market Position entirely) forces at least 'revise', an empty positioning forces 'hold'. This is the deterministic backbone of the verdict.

position_authored.description: Whether sources/market-position.yaml exists and is schema-valid.

missing.description: Required positioning answers that are absent or empty (e.g. commercial_promise.pay_trigger, reader_segment.primary).

internal.description: Does the positioning agree with the authored Novel Brain? Deterministic cross-reads: channel match, whether the Brain's promise/target_reader are consistent with the Position's segment and pay trigger. Contradictions lower the recommendation but never below what completeness allows.

conflicts.description: Deterministic Brain/Position disagreements found (e.g. channel mismatch, empty overlap between Brain.target_reader.avoids and Position.drop_triggers is fine, but a Brain forbidden_style that the Position leans on is flagged).

external.description: Does the positioning agree with the derived Market Snapshot (the real market read)? Deterministic cross-reads: is the Position's channel present in the snapshot, do its leaned-on tropes / genre align with trending_genres, are its stated drop_triggers informed by the snapshot's common_drop_points. Absent snapshot degrades to advisory-only (never a conflict), and a STALE snapshot is surfaced but never gates.

snapshot_stale.description: Mirrors the Market Snapshot's staleness.is_stale; surfaced but advisory (never gates).

alignments.description: Where the Position aligns with the market read (e.g. a leaned-on genre appears in trending_genres; a drop_trigger matches a common_drop_point).

misalignments.description: Where the Position ignores the market read (e.g. targets a channel with no snapshot signal). Advisory — lowers to 'revise' at most, never 'hold' on its own.

sources.description: Pins to the inputs this verdict folded, for auditability/reproducibility.

rationale.description: Human-readable summary of why this recommendation was made.
